FINDING_ID: IM_F001
SEVERITY: 0.89
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82
DESCRIPTION: `record_model_round()` treats any round with `failed=False` and `response_chars > 2000` plus `finding_count == 0` as a parser-yield pathology, even when the zero findings are simply due to a FORMAT failure that was already classified elsewhere. In the shown architecture, `failed` is just a boolean from manager integration, not the actual `FailureType`. A parseable but format-noncompliant response can therefore be counted simultaneously as “not failed” for parser-yield purposes and as a protocol failure in `FailureHandler`. That creates a false secondary diagnosis: the immune layer blames the parser/extractor when the primary defect was output-format violation. This is a boundary bug between `FailureHandler` and `DetectorHealthMonitor`: the immune monitor lacks the typed failure context needed to avoid misclassifying protocol failures as parser failures.
PROPOSED_FIX: Change `record_model_round()` to accept the concrete `failure_type: Optional[FailureType]` rather than only `failed: bool`, and suppress parser-yield detection when `failure_type` is `FORMAT`, `MALFORMED`, `EMPTY`, or `TIMEOUT`. More generally, split “0 findings with substantive response” into mutually exclusive categories based on typed failure context.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F002
SEVERITY: 0.86
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78
DESCRIPTION: `record_model_round()` appends zero-valued telemetry for failed rounds into `_model_response_times`, `_model_response_chars`, and `_model_finding_history`, and later uses those same histories for monotonic-decline and cost-per-finding anomaly detection without failure-state filtering. This means transport/protocol failures contaminate productivity histories: e.g. a timeout round recorded as `finding_count=0` can help trigger `monotonic_decline`, and repeated failed rounds can reshape the per-model baseline that later CPF checks compare against. That conflates “model unavailable / protocol failure” with “model productively responding but deteriorating,” causing the immune layer to diagnose prompt/decomposition pathologies from infrastructure failures.
PROPOSED_FIX: Track failure-state alongside each per-model round record, or maintain separate histories for successful rounds versus failed rounds. Exclude failed rounds from monotonic-decline and CPF baseline calculations unless the pathology is explicitly intended to model failures rather than productivity.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F003
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74
DESCRIPTION: `record_round()` assumes `_vocab_growth_history` is synchronized one-to-one with `_finding_counts`, but that coupling is only an external calling convention (`record_vocab_growth()` is “called by manager”). There is no round index, no length check against `_finding_counts`, and no guard that the last vocab-growth value belongs to the current round. If the manager misses a call, calls twice, or calls in the wrong order, the vocab-saturation detector will pair stale or shifted vocab-growth samples with current finding counts and emit diagnoses against the wrong round. This is a concrete interface defect inside the immune boundary because the monitor stores two independent append-only streams and then assumes temporal alignment without encoding it.
PROPOSED_FIX: Make vocab growth part of `record_round()` inputs, or store `(round_idx, value)` tuples and validate alignment before using `_vocab_growth_history[-n:]` with `_finding_counts[-n:]`. Reject or skip saturation detection on misaligned telemetry.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F004
SEVERITY: 0.81
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76
DESCRIPTION: `record_model_round()` can emit multiple unrelated pathologies for the same underlying failure episode in one call because its detectors are not mutually constrained. A single round can increment `model_failure`, then also trigger `monotonic_decline` from the trailing zeros in finding history, and later influence CPF or parser-yield logic. This creates an immune overcounting problem: one failure mode fans out into several diagnoses with distinct recommended actions, even though those diagnoses are not conditionally independent. The subsystem lacks a precedence policy among model-level pathologies analogous to the priority ordering in `FailureHandler`.
PROPOSED_FIX: Add typed per-round failure context and short-circuit lower-confidence productivity detectors when a higher-priority model failure is active for that round or within the recent lookback. Model-level immune checks should have precedence rules mirroring the failure taxonomy.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F005
SEVERITY: 0.79
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69
DESCRIPTION: The self-diagnosis path for high false positive rate directly mutates `_sensitivity_decay`, but unlike the low-success path it performs no actual P-pass through `_p_pass_self_adjustment()` or any equivalent gate. The docstring says “All self-adjustments are logged and P-passed,” yet this branch applies immediately after only a local trend heuristic. This is a missed inconsistency distinct from the known “parameter has no runtime effect” issue: even if `effective_window()` were fixed, this branch would still bypass the subsystem’s stated safety gate for self-modification.
PROPOSED_FIX: Route all self-adjustments, including single-parameter ones, through a common self-adjustment P-pass function that records approval/rejection rationale and enforces damping/bounds consistently.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F006
SEVERITY: 0.77
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71
DESCRIPTION: `recommended_chain_start()` learns step effectiveness from `pathology_key`, but `record_natural_resolution()` and large parts of pathology counting operate on detector names or ad hoc keys that do not normalize to the same namespace. The subsystem is therefore mixing at least three identity schemes: detector names (`"kappa"`), remediation chain keys (`"kappa_stuck"`), and per-model pathology keys (`"model_failure_m1"`). Even where individual mismatches are already known, the broader missed defect is architectural: the immune layer has no canonical pathology identifier, so learning, resolution accounting, chain skipping, and active-remediation tracking are inherently brittle across all detectors.
PROPOSED_FIX: Introduce a canonical pathology ID enum/schema carried in every `DetectorDiagnosis` and use it consistently for `_pathology_counts`, `_resolved_counts`, `_false_positive_history`, `_remediation_state`, `_step_effectiveness`, and chain lookup. Keep human-readable `pathology` text separate from machine identity.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F007
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66
DESCRIPTION: `chain_exhaustion_rate` mixes incompatible units: `_remediation_outcomes` is step-level data while `_chain_exhaustion_history` is chain-level data. The denominator `len(recent_outcomes) + len(recent_exhaustions)` therefore combines “number of verified steps” with “number of exhausted chains,” so the resulting rate is not a meaningful fraction of encounters that exhausted their chain. This is separate from the known double-count concern: even without double-counting, the metric is dimensionally wrong and can mis-trigger self-diagnosis.
PROPOSED_FIX: Compute exhaustion rate over chain encounters only. Track a pathology encounter/attempt ID from first application through success or exhaustion, then define exhaustion rate as exhausted_encounters / total_completed_encounters over a consistent recent window.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F008
SEVERITY: 0.72
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73
DESCRIPTION: `check_dispatch_health()` takes `round_idx` as an argument but does not use it to window, deduplicate, or validate the supplied histories. That indicates an interface/ownership defect: the function signature implies round-local evaluation, but the implementation re-scans full historical lists every call and relies on internal side effects in `_pathology_counts` to avoid exact duplicates. This makes the caller contract ambiguous and fragile, especially because block/success histories are external to the monitor and can be replayed or reordered.
PROPOSED_FIX: Either remove `round_idx` from the interface and document that the function consumes cumulative histories idempotently, or use `round_idx` to process only new events since the last check with explicit cursor state.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F009
SEVERITY: 0.70
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64
DESCRIPTION: `record_model_round()` hardcodes the escalation trigger for consecutive model failures at `consecutive >= 2` instead of using the configured failure repetition threshold `n_fail`. That creates two inconsistent notions of persistence inside the same immune/failure subsystem: `FailureHandler.get_recovery()` consults `config.n_fail`, while the immune detector emits `model_failure` diagnoses on its own fixed threshold. The result is that the monitor can diagnose chronic model failure before or after the recovery policy considers it repeated, depending on config.
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass the relevant config into `DetectorHealthMonitor` or inject the threshold explicitly so model-failure pathology detection uses the same `n_fail` semantics as `FailureHandler`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F010
SEVERITY: 0.68
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61
DESCRIPTION: The immune layer has no explicit representation of “diagnosis suppressed because a stronger explanation already exists.” As a result, downstream meta-metrics such as `false_positive_rate`, diagnosis counts, and self-diagnosis operate on raw emitted diagnoses only, not on a curated set of causally distinct pathology episodes. This is not just duplication noise; it means the layer cannot distinguish detector over-triggering from correct hierarchical diagnosis of a single incident. The absence of a suppression/causal-link mechanism undermines the claimed self-assessment metrics.
PROPOSED_FIX: Add an incident/episode model with primary vs secondary diagnoses and suppression reasons. Meta-metrics should operate on primary pathology episodes or weighted diagnoses, not on every emitted diagnosis equally.
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: IM_F011
SEVERITY: 0.66
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` emits events for EMPTY/TIMEOUT/MALFORMED/FORMAT but not for UNDERPERFORM, while `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_model_round()` has no event callback and silently produces model-level pathologies. The immune boundary therefore has split observability: some failure signals are available in the manager event stream and others only in internal diagnosis state. This is an interface inconsistency for operators and any external monitoring that expects a unified stream of immune-relevant anomalies.
PROPOSED_FIX: Standardize emission: either all failure/immune diagnoses should be representable as `ManagerEvent`s, or the event stream contract should explicitly exclude immune-only detections and expose a parallel query interface. Prefer emitting UNDERPERFORM and immune diagnoses as typed events.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F012
SEVERITY: 0.64
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57
DESCRIPTION: `record_round()` uses `len(self._mu_history) >= eff_mu_window + 1` and then requires every consecutive pair in that window to exceed a 10% rise threshold. For negative or near-zero `mu`, this predicate becomes unstable: very small oscillations around zero can fail or pass based on tiny absolute differences, while sustained harmful drift that is slower than 10% per step is ignored. This is distinct from existing findings about sign handling and count persistence; the missed issue is the detector’s pathologically scale-sensitive use of percentage growth on a metric that can cross zero.
PROPOSED_FIX: Detect `mu` pathology using a signed/absolute hybrid criterion with an epsilon floor, e.g. compare rolling means or require monotone deterioration in a stabilized transformed metric rather than percentage change relative to the previous point.
VERIFIED: TRUE

Definitive stance: the strongest missed issues are the failure-type/context loss between `FailureHandler` and `DetectorHealthMonitor`, telemetry-stream misalignment for vocab growth, and inconsistent gating of self-adjustments. These are additive to the prior findings and materially affect immune-layer correctness.
